sources.title: GGPEN satellite mission control centre (MCC)
sources.locator: Capacidade para operar até três satélites em simultâneo, including the list of MCC functions

quantities.quantity: Maximum number of satellites the centre can operate simultaneously

sources.conditions: The Angolan ground control centre monitors the ANGOSAT-2 telecommunications satellite. Its continuous monitoring is a ground-service capability.
sources.supports: A precedent for recording subsystem telemetry and diagnosing faults from a control room.
sources.limits: The source contains no public rover hardware specifications, rover fault-response times or Earth–Moon communications link budget.

sources.title: CONAE deep-space stations and receiver specifications
sources.locator: Section 6, Detalle del Equipamiento Disponible, Estación CLTC-CONAE-NEUQUEN, (a) Antena y receptores
sources.conditions: Ground receive equipment at the Argentina–China Neuquén station. The page also lists a different station at Malargüe.
sources.supports: A real ground endpoint for lunar communications planning. The listed receive bands can be checked against a proposed transmitting system.
sources.limits: A ground antenna specification supplies neither a rover transmit power nor an available relay, data rate or coverage guarantee.

sources.title: Argentina reports tracking support for Chinese lunar and Mars missions
sources.locator: Paragraph beginning «La Estación CLTC-CONAE-NEUQUÉN brindó soporte»
sources.conditions: Argentina's account of ground support to Chang’e and Tianwen-1 through the joint Neuquén station.
sources.supports: Distinguishes an actual deep-space ground-support contribution from ownership of the lunar and Mars rover vehicles.
sources.limits: This account does not specify a direct radio link between a rover and Neuquén, contact durations, or rover radio characteristics.

sources.title: Bahrain’s report to COPUOS on navigation cameras for Rashid Rover 3
sources.locator: A/AC.105/1337, Bahrain submission dated 27 October 2024, p. 6, Space segment, paragraph 1(c)
sources.role: lunar rover navigation payload under development

quantities.quantity: Navigation cameras in Bahrain's Rashid Rover 3 contribution

sources.conditions: Bahrain's national submission describes collaboration with the UAE's Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre on the Rashid Rover 3 lunar mission.
sources.supports: A direct example of navigation and science cameras supplied by a partner to a lunar rover.
sources.limits: Bahrain supplied the camera development effort. The report gives no camera field of view, stereo baseline, hazard detection accuracy, or surface performance.

sources.title: Bahrain’s 2025 update on lunar surface and orbital instruments
sources.locator: A/AC.105/1367, Bahrain submission dated 21 October 2025, p. 3, final two paragraphs of Space segment
sources.role: lunar rover navigation payload development update
sources.conditions: Bahrain reported developing the four surface-rover cameras. A separate joint hyperspectral instrument with Egypt is intended for a lunar orbiter.
sources.supports: Distinguishes the navigation camera contribution from orbital mineral and ice mapping.
sources.limits: The submission describes planned mounting and launch. It supplies no in-situ imagery or camera acceptance-test data.

sources.title: AEB 2023 management report on Brazil’s integration and test facility
sources.locator: Printed p. 61, Laboratório de Integração e Testes (LIT), text above Figure 31

quantities.quantity: Reported upper satellite mass for the facility's integration and environmental tests

sources.conditions: AEB describes INPE's Brazilian satellite integration facility and lists thermal-vacuum, electromagnetic, vibration, acoustic, shock and mass-property work.
sources.supports: A documented precedent for checking structure, mass properties, electronics and thermal response with complementary tests.
sources.limits: This is a laboratory satellite mass limit. The source contains no qualifying test result or mass requirement for a planetary rover.

sources.title: Brazilian space programme test facility, INPE LIT thermal-vacuum laboratory
sources.locator: Principais Meios de Testes, item (a), Câmara de Simulação Espacial 6m x 8m
sources.conditions: The facility operator INPE specifies a high-vacuum chamber with a zoned thermal shroud. AEB identifies this facility in its programme report (aeb-01).
sources.supports: Defines an example equipment envelope for a future subsystem thermal-vacuum test.
sources.limits: Chamber capability alone establishes no rover survival temperature, test cycle, or qualification result.

sources.title: NASRDA Centre for Space Transport and Propulsion reports structural integration and test work
sources.locator: Technical Divisions at CSTP & Activities, sections 2 (Structural Integration Systems) and 4 (Project Division)
sources.conditions: Ground and flight preparation for a Nigerian rocket test in April 2019 included integration at CSTP and final checks on the launch platform.
sources.supports: An example of separating fabrication, integrated checks, and safety and quality-control responsibilities in a test plan.
sources.limits: This was a rocket integration exercise. No public rover specification, rover load case, measured vibration spectrum or planetary traction result was identified in this record.

sources.title: GuaraniSat-2 mechanical properties and payload distribution
sources.locator: 17 July 2025 drawing presentation, p. 2, Satellite properties, and p. 3, Isometric view (deployed configuration)

quantities.quantity: GuaraniSat-2 total mass listed in the drawing

sources.conditions: AEP publishes separate bare-structure and overall stowed dimensions for the satellite. Its table specifies hardcoat-anodized 6061-T6 aluminum for the structure.
sources.supports: Demonstrates why a payload drawing records the overall envelope and explicit stowed/deployed configuration as well as mass.
sources.limits: A CubeSat drawing is an integration example. It supplies no public rover chassis dimensions, structural load rating or flight qualification for its use on a rover.

sources.title: Paraguay’s COPUOS report on its deployed GuaraniSat-1 and planned sensor telemetry
sources.locator: Republic of Paraguay statement, 2021 legal subcommittee, agenda item 3, pp. 3–5
sources.conditions: Paraguay reported the March 2021 orbital deployment of GuaraniSat-1 and described plans for communicating field detector data through the satellite.
sources.supports: An example of specifying the sensor, ground terminal and spacecraft as separate endpoints when designing telemetry.
sources.limits: The statement records orbital deployment. It gives no measured link throughput, detector yield, or rover communications specification.

sources.title: Agence Sénégalaise d’Études Spatiales — agency mandate
sources.locator: PDF p. 36, ASES back-cover notice citing decree 2023-754
sources.conditions: Senegalese agency notice published in the national press agency magazine in 2024.
sources.supports: Establishes ASES’s policy, research and training mandate. It identifies the institution represented in the partner roster.
sources.limits: No rover hardware, cabin specification or fire experiment is described.

sources.title: SENSAT — GAINDESAT-1A
sources.locator: Fiche technique and Comment ça fonctionne, including Balises au sol, Collecte en orbite and Transmission
sources.conditions: Senegal’s SENSAT programme describes an Earth-orbiting CubeSat launched on 16 August 2024 to collect and relay environmental data from ground stations.
sources.supports: Documents national experience with telemetry and orbital data collection. The source is a SENSAT programme record.
sources.limits: Orbital satellite data cannot establish a planetary rover’s mass, wheels, atmosphere or fire response. No applicable public ASES rover specification was identified in the reviewed sources.

sources.title: Agencia Espacial Española — Relaciones internacionales y bilaterales
sources.locator: Programas bilaterales, paragraph headed Colaboración con la NASA
sources.conditions: AEE attributes the HGAS antennas and the MEDA and REMS weather instruments on NASA’s Perseverance and Curiosity to Spain.
sources.supports: Establishes Spain’s contribution to flown Mars rovers. CAB (CSIC–INTA) led MEDA as detailed in aee-02.
sources.limits: The agency record attributes a national contribution. It supplies no complete rover or fire-system design.

sources.title: CAB (CSIC–INTA) — MEDA envía el primer informe meteorológico desde el cráter Jezero en Marte
sources.locator: PDF pp. 1–3, instrument description, first reading, and sols 43–44

quantities.quantity: Approximate measured wind gust for sols 43–44

sources.conditions: The CAB-led suite flew on NASA’s Perseverance. Weather observations cover Jezero crater on 3–4 April 2021, ahead of the Ingenuity flight.
sources.supports: Constrains an exposed Mars environmental sensor payload and provides an example of time- and site-specific weather data.
sources.limits: The reported weather is local and outside the rover. A cabin temperature, ventilation rate, fire threshold or qualification range cannot be inferred.

sources.title: Türkiye Uzay Ajansı — 2025 Performans Programı
sources.locator: Printed p. 16 (PDF p. 20), performance indicator 2 for the lunar soft-landing project, explanatory paragraph
sources.conditions: TUA describes the AYAP-2 soft-landing phase and preliminary work, including student teams, on a planned mobile rover.
sources.supports: Establishes a planned lunar surface mobility activity in the second phase and the maturity of the public evidence.
sources.limits: Programme completion percentages are administrative indicators. The document gives no measured rover mass, payload, speed or cabin values.

sources.title: Türkiye Uzay Ajansı — Türkiye’nin Ay Yolculuğunda Geri Sayım Başladı
sources.locator: 16 September 2026 announcement, paragraphs on integration, environmental testing and lunar orbit
sources.conditions: The first Turkish deep-space spacecraft had completed assembly and integration and entered the system-level environmental test phase.
sources.supports: Separates current phase-one spacecraft testing from the second-phase rover proposal in tua-01.
sources.limits: The orbital spacecraft’s test programme and mass supply no ground mobility or cabin fire data for a rover.

sources.title: Turkish Space Agency — AYAP-1
sources.locator: Projects → Ongoing Projects → AYAP-1, programme objective
sources.conditions: TUA frames lunar surface mobility as an objective of the overall Lunar Research Programme.
sources.supports: Provides an English-language agency pointer to the programme. The detailed performance plan identifies the rover with its second phase.
sources.limits: The page title alone does not establish phase-one rover hardware or surface operations.

sources.title: MBRSC team — The Rashid rover: to guide the way for the next generation lunar missions and solar system exploration
sources.locator: EGU 2021, first PDF page, rover specifications table, Mobility row
sources.conditions: MBRSC’s mission engineers presented the Rashid-1 preflight design in 2021. The differential drive was intended to operate during lunar daylight.
sources.supports: Supplies engineering targets for comparison with a small, uncrewed, exposed rover.
sources.limits: This preflight configuration differs from the later dimensional summary in mbrsc-02. No successful surface operation confirmed these design targets.

sources.title: Protocol Department of Dubai — Rashid 1 landing outcome and Rashid 2 announcement
sources.locator: 26 April 2023, paragraphs on HAKUTO-R, the first Emirates Lunar Mission and the dimensions of the first rover
sources.conditions: MBRSC built the first Rashid rover. Its HAKUTO-R carrier reached lunar orbit and the landing attempt on 25 April 2023 failed.
sources.supports: Provides a government summary of approximate flight-vehicle dimensions and mission outcome.
sources.limits: The dimensions refer to Rashid 1. Its lunar wheel performance, internal temperatures and survival time were never measured on the surface.

sources.title: Hurrell et al. — Traction Performance Evaluation for a Rashid-1 Rover Wheel
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4–6, §2.1 Single-Wheel Experiment, figures 1–3; §§3–4 for experiment versus simulation
sources.conditions: The authors measured traction, sinkage and tracks using a rigid test wheel on a terrestrial rig, with loosely packed simulant at about 25% relative density. The flight wheel had an open structure and shorter grousers.
sources.supports: Provides a component-level test method with declared loads, wheel geometry and slip conditions suitable for planning a validation experiment.
sources.limits: Predicted performance at lunar gravity came from simulation. The ground wheel differed from flight hardware. These results supply no cabin fire data.

sources.title: Firefly Aerospace — Blue Ghost Mission 2 manifest
sources.locator: Mission Summary and Rashid Rover 2 payload section
sources.conditions: Firefly lists MBRSC’s Rashid Rover 2 on an upcoming lunar far-side delivery targeted no earlier than 2027 in the manifest reviewed in November 2026.
sources.supports: Identifies a planned wheel-material exposure experiment on the Moon’s far side.
sources.limits: The announced test objective provides no measured durability or abrasion result.

sources.title: Korea AeroSpace Administration — 원격 제어를 넘어 ‘자율 주행’을 위한 우주탐사 모빌리티에 AI 도입 추진
sources.locator: 24 June 2026 press release no. 427, second and third body paragraphs, including ‘달의 낮 기간(14일 이내)’

quantities.quantity: Upper bound on the described lunar daytime operating period

sources.conditions: KASA described its planned 2032 landing mission at an expert meeting on autonomous navigation and payload support.
sources.supports: Documents a daylight mission concept and trade-offs between route energy and hazard avoidance.
sources.limits: The quoted interval is a planning window. It supplies no measured battery endurance, night survival or flight-qualified specification.

sources.title: Wang, Kim and Han — Experimental Analysis of Lunar Rover Wheel’s Mobility Performance Depending on Soil Condition and Wheel Configuration
sources.locator: §§3.1–3.4 (tables 2–4), §4.1 (figures 5–6), §4.2 (wheel comparisons)

quantities.quantity: Grouser height in the cross-soil comparison

sources.conditions: The KICT researchers used a single-wheel terrestrial rig with KLS-1 Korean lunar simulant and Jumunjin sand. They compared drawbar pull, torque and sinkage under controlled slip.
sources.supports: Provides an engineering test matrix showing that the same wheel responds differently to soil and grouser geometry.
sources.limits: Research published in 2017 predates KASA. It is not a KASA-run test or a measurement of the planned national flight rover.

sources.title: UK Space Agency — Mission to explore life on Mars one step closer as UK team to replace Russian components for Mars Rover
sources.locator: 23 November 2023, paragraphs on Airbus Stevenage, Enfys and the drill sampling depth

quantities.quantity: Approximate intended maximum subsurface sampling depth

sources.conditions: Airbus built Rosalind Franklin in Stevenage for ESA’s mission. UKSA funded the Aberystwyth-led Enfys instrument to select sampling targets. The drill depth is an overall rover system capability.
sources.supports: Supports a sampling-tool reach requirement and documents the roles of UKSA, Airbus and the instrument team.
sources.limits: The depth is a design capability. The source does not report a drilling operation on Mars or attribute construction of the drill to the UK team.

sources.title: UK Space Agency — Airbus Defence and Space opens state-of-the-art Mars Yard
sources.locator: 27 March 2014 announcement, paragraph containing Colin Paynter’s statement on the enlarged facility

quantities.quantity: Specially selected sand in the test arena

sources.conditions: UKSA describes the Airbus ground-test facility in Stevenage where the ExoMars team could evaluate autonomous navigation in an enclosed analogue.
sources.supports: Offers a dimensional reference for a terrain and navigation test course.
sources.limits: The ground facility dimensions do not give a rover’s maximum climb angle or performance on Mars. Mission dates forecast in this historical announcement are obsolete.

sources.title: Moon Base Phases
sources.locator: Lunar Terrain Vehicles, crew/cargo capacity and control modes
sources.role: NASA commissions commercial crew and cargo surface mobility for the lunar south pole.
sources.conditions: Planned open lunar vehicles, Astrolab CLV-1 and Lunar Outpost Pegasus. Crews wear pressure suits.
sources.supports: Model an unpressurized transport with crew seats, cargo space and remote or onboard driving.
sources.limits: Source does not publish an occupied pressure vessel, free air volume, design mass, or combustible inventory for these vehicles.

sources.title: Perseverance Rover Components
sources.locator: Body: Tech Specs; Wheels and Legs: Tech Specs – Wheels; How the Wheels Move
sources.role: NASA and JPL provide flight rover geometry, mass, wheel dimensions, steering and suspension descriptions.
sources.conditions: As-built robotic Mars rover. Exterior dimensions are rounded; the rock-sampling arm extends outside the body.
sources.supports: Set a scale for a six-wheel imaging and sample-collection chassis and illustrate equipment deck, robotic arm and rocker-bogie suspension.
sources.limits: Dimensions bound the whole rover. They do not specify a pressure-vessel volume, crew atmosphere, mass of an individual part, or fire response.

sources.title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires
sources.locator: ICES-2021-266, Table 2, Flight-Sample V-2 column; section III.A and Figure 3
sources.role: NASA Glenn and partners conducted orbital fuel burns in uncrewed Cygnus and measured thin-fabric flame size.
sources.conditions: Saffire V sample 2, cotton jersey, orbital microgravity, forced coflow; the fan was stopped and later restarted. The flame recovered when ventilation resumed.
sources.supports: Use as an observed flame-size reference at the reported material, atmosphere, flow and size. Keep flame size separate from distance burned and spread speed.
sources.limits: Not a partial-gravity rover cabin burn. Changing gravity, material construction, ventilation or mounting breaks direct equivalence. It supplies no whole-cabin heat-release law.

sources.title: Lunar Terrain Vehicle
sources.locator: Lunar Terrain Vehicle Commercial Companies: Astrolab and Lunar Outpost
sources.role: NASA identifies the two LTV providers and their individual lunar vehicle designs.
sources.conditions: NASA public program overview, accessed November 2026. Images include mockups or renderings.
sources.supports: Identify Astrolab CLV-1 and Lunar Outpost Pegasus as separate open crew-transport designs.
sources.limits: Images are not surveyed blueprints or flight measurements. They do not establish cabin air, material properties, electrical loads or exact component positions.

sources.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test
sources.locator: Sections II and III; Table I, Mylar G at 10.2 psia column; Figure 5
sources.role: NASA reports short-duration partial-gravity flammability tests and separates the surviving and extinguishing oxygen concentrations.

quantities.quantity: Martian-g lowest tested oxygen with sustained flame (ULOI*)
Martian-g highest tested oxygen with extinction (MOC*)
lunar-g lowest tested oxygen with sustained flame (ULOI*)
lunar-g highest tested oxygen with extinction (MOC*)

sources.conditions: Mylar G film; hot-wire ignition; buoyant upward spread under simulated partial gravity in a centrifuge aboard a drop-tower rig. Starred limits use flame survival to the end of a short test.
sources.supports: Compare a single material and pressure under two gravity levels and distinguish tested oxygen brackets from long-duration material qualification.
sources.limits: Earlier lunar results are reproduced in the paper. Different exposure times, surface geometry, forced flow, pressure or fuel can change the bracket. Not a transferable cabin cutoff, spread rate or certification.

sources.title: Canada's Contribution to Mars Science Laboratory
sources.locator: The Maple Leaf on Mars: Canada's Contribution, APXS measurement sequence
sources.role: CSA provided the arm-mounted APXS instrument on Curiosity and funded its operations centre.
sources.conditions: Canadian prelanding engineering description of bringing the sensor head close to a soil or rock target and integrating X-ray counts.
sources.supports: Support an externally mounted contact-science instrument and differentiate a quick survey from a full analysis.
sources.limits: These are approximate integration times, dependent on measurement objectives. They do not specify motor energy, interior fuel, component mass or fire properties.

sources.title: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin (RFM)
sources.locator: Mission overview; ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Rover; Drilling in brief
sources.role: ESA leads the rover mission and describes its mobility, sample acquisition and onboard delivery system.

quantities.quantity: extension rods needed for full reach

sources.conditions: Planned solar-powered Mars surface mission. Each wheel has independent steering and drive.
sources.supports: Represent a robotic mobile drilling lab with flexible wheels, extension rods, sample handling and orbital data relay.
sources.limits: Mission design values do not give measured Mars drilling performance, human-cabin dimensions, or rover fire measurements.

sources.title: First deep drilling success for ExoMars
sources.locator: Opening account; Drill operations; No easy feat
sources.role: ESA reports a sample retrieval by its ground twin at the ALTEC Mars Terrain Simulator in Turin.
sources.conditions: A gravity-offloaded rover test model on Earth sampled medium-hard cemented clay in a layered test well.
sources.supports: Provide a measured drill demonstration with substitute terrain and a sample transferred into the rover laboratory.
sources.limits: The rig offloaded vehicle weight. It did not reproduce the complete Mars environment or prove the same depth on Mars.

sources.title: Chandrayaan-3 Details
sources.locator: Overall specifications: Mass, Power generation, Communication; Rover Payloads
sources.role: ISRO publishes the mass, power generation rating, communications path and instrument list for the Chandrayaan-3 rover.
sources.conditions: Lunar robotic rover, designed for one lunar day. Relays data through the lander. Rover payloads include APXS and LIBS.
sources.supports: Provide a compact lunar rover comparison and distinguish electrical power generation in watts from battery storage in watt-hours.
sources.limits: The 50 W value is a generation rating. This source does not give time-resolved output, battery storage, a crew cabin or material flammability.

sources.title: ExoMars
sources.locator: Italian contribution, MA_MISS; International agreements, drilling system
sources.role: ASI describes Italian instrument and industrial contributions, including INAF-IAPS collaboration on Ma_MISS in the drill.
sources.conditions: ExoMars payload design: observe the borehole wall spectroscopically during drilling.
sources.supports: Support an Italian drill-integrated sensor that interrogates layers in place and distinguishes a sensor in the drill from a camera on the mast.
sources.limits: Historical ASI page contains superseded launch dates. Use this source for payload architecture; drill depth is design reach, and no borehole data from Mars is reported here.

sources.title: Inside development of the crewed pressurized rover for Artemis (JAXA engineering interview, in Japanese)
sources.locator: 31 March 2026; section 過酷な月面でも宇宙飛行士が快適に過ごせるように, answers on thermal control and environmental control
sources.role: JAXA’s habitat thermal and life-support engineer describes the pressurized rover being developed with Toyota.
sources.conditions: Preliminary design reported in March 2026. Cabin environmental systems regulate pressure, temperature and humidity and remove CO₂. Insulation, pumps and radiators help manage heat.
sources.supports: Distinguish the occupied pressure vessel and its actively controlled atmosphere from an open vehicle or a sealed passive test box.
sources.limits: Public interview offers no cabin pressure setpoint, O₂ fraction, ventilation rate, free gas volume, internal material inventory or validated fire response.

sources.title: JAXA and Toyota Reach Agreement on Consideration Toward International Space Exploration
sources.locator: 12 March 2019; Concept proposal for the pressurized rover being studied by JAXA and Toyota
sources.role: JAXA and Toyota jointly describe their early lunar pressurized rover concept.
sources.conditions: Historical concept dimensions as of March 2019. Toyota hosted this joint announcement, which identifies JAXA as a coauthor.
sources.supports: Compare the scale of an early crewed lunar concept to a robotic chassis and distinguish living space from the vehicle bounding box.
sources.limits: The 13 m³ figure describes proposed living space. Effective free gas volume, final flight geometry, atmosphere, heat removal, and actual component masses require independent evidence.

sources.title: 2026 Space Agency Partners
sources.locator: 2026 Space Agency Partners, 17 agency tiles
sources.conditions: 2026 edition, retrieved 15 November 2026.
sources.supports: Determines register membership.
sources.limits: Event participation gives no endorsement, hardware supply or test approval.

sources.title: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle
sources.locator: Opening mission summary and following chassis and wheel descriptions
sources.conditions: Open electric vehicle carrying suited Apollo astronauts on lunar EVA.
sources.supports: Flown lunar mobility and purpose of the wire-mesh wheel.
sources.limits: Original frame and wheel figures describe Apollo hardware only.

sources.title: NBS Technical Note 1128, heats of combustion
sources.locator: Table 1, printed p. 66, PDF p. 78
sources.conditions: Table of common materials. Oxygen volume column is referenced to 25 °C. Net heat is per mass of fuel.
sources.supports: Energy accounting on the assumption the specified dry mass reacts completely.
sources.limits: Generic substances. No coupon-lot measurement, speed, heat flux to a wall, ignition or extinction limit.

sources.title: Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, revision 2
sources.locator: Table 3-24, PDF p. 63
sources.conditions: HIDH reference crew and daily activity schedule, modeled metabolic loads. Aerobic interval in source schedule is 0.5 h.
sources.supports: Sizing a constant-activity interval.
sources.limits: Not an individual crew measurement or a multi-day exercise prescription. No regulator capacity stated.

sources.title: Evaluating Extravehicular Activity Access Options for a Lunar Surface Habitat
sources.locator: NTRS abstract, comparison of three EVA access options
sources.conditions: Lunar habitat trade study, including an air-save system and a suitport-airlock maintained in vacuum.
sources.supports: Different cycled gas volumes and gas recovery architectures.
sources.limits: Published abstract supplies no measured leak rate or suitport dead volume for this design.

sources.title: Small Spacecraft Technology State of the Art, Thermal Control
sources.locator: Section 7.1, equation 1 and Figure 7.1, printed p. 205
sources.conditions: Spacecraft radiation exchange, solar absorption and heat generation.
sources.supports: Separates solar projection from infrared-emitting area in a steady panel budget.
sources.limits: The teaching case omits convection, conduction, transient storage and a resolved view-factor model.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-008, Fire Protection
sources.locator: PDF pp. 8–10, Fire Detection, Fire Suppression, Post-Fire Monitoring
sources.conditions: Human spaceflight guidance for equipment bays, cabin and ventilation-return detectors and crew access to extinguishers.
sources.supports: Use release and sampling location as separate controls. Track agent and post-fire cleanup.
sources.limits: No calibration of a tracer alarm or extinguishing dose for this hybrid.

sources.title: Development of the ISS Fine Water Mist Portable Fire Extinguisher
sources.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract
sources.conditions: Engineering-development abstract comparing ISS extinguisher types and microgravity design issues.
sources.supports: Water-mist technology as a component family.
sources.limits: No extracted discharge curve, electrical suitability or installed-system extinguishment tests.

sources.title: Whatman filtration product guide
sources.locator: PDF p. 16, Technical specifications, Qualitative filter papers—standard grades, grade 1
sources.conditions: Nominal properties for commercial qualitative filter paper, grade 1.
sources.supports: A candidate source of identifiable cellulose-rich lab stock and a check against weighing and measuring the lot.
sources.limits: No fire values or flight material qualification. No purchased lot assumed.

sources.title: Product handling information, Polystone G HD natural extruded, 590976
sources.locator: PDF p. 1, §2 Product details
sources.conditions: PE-HD/PE 300 semifinished product. Product lists stabilizer and additives.
sources.supports: Traceable candidate grade for a sourced PE coupon.
sources.limits: Additives prevent equating stock with a pure CH2 repeat unit for an installed fire test.

sources.title: NASA-STD-6001 status record
sources.locator: Document Identifiers and Document Scope
sources.conditions: Standards registry lists revision B with change 3.
sources.supports: Identifies the active revision used for this research.
sources.limits: Applicability depends on the program and material configuration.

sources.title: NASA-STD-6001B with Change 3
sources.conditions: Worst-case anticipated atmosphere, bottom ignition, vertical specimens, one specimen per test, subject to applicable standard provisions.
sources.supports: Gives a concrete comparison protocol and highlights geometry and atmosphere.
sources.limits: This archive contains no such qualification report for the proposed assembly.

sources.title: Moon Facts
sources.locator: Structure, surface and atmosphere sections, including sunlit/dark temperatures
sources.conditions: Lunar surface in sunlight or darkness. Local latitude, shadow and exposure affect temperature.
sources.supports: Demonstrates why illumination and external thermal boundary are separate controls.
sources.limits: Surface temperature does not determine radiator sink temperature or cabin gas temperature.

sources.title: Mars Facts
sources.locator: Atmosphere and Surface
sources.conditions: Thin CO2-dominated Martian atmosphere and varying surface temperature.
sources.supports: Mars requires a distinct external pressure and radiative boundary.
sources.limits: No site weather time series or pressure-vessel performance.

sources.title: What Is Microgravity?
sources.locator: Why do astronauts float in space? Explanation of orbital free fall
sources.conditions: Spacecraft and occupants freely fall together in orbit.
sources.supports: Use ideal zero support force in an unrestrained orbit case.
sources.limits: An accelerometer measures specific force; a lone reading cannot infer world or distinguish all motions.

sources.title: PSI-98 Saffire-I original experimental table
sources.locator: CSV rows 2–3, sample S1 and S2, columns Air Flow, Percent O2 and Flow Direction
sources.conditions: SIBAL fabric in orbital microgravity. S1 concurrent and S2 opposed. Same specimen reused.
sources.supports: A real controlled-flow comparator with material, atmosphere and direction recorded.
sources.limits: Velocity in a test duct is not whole-cabin volume flow. The CSV does not give a cabin detector threshold.

sources.title: Large-scale spacecraft fire safety experiments, SIBAL results
sources.locator: Slide 21, SIBAL Fabric Results, 40.6-cm-wide sample
sources.conditions: Orbital Saffire-I, wide cotton/fiberglass specimen, 20 cm/s airflow. PSI-98 identifies differing initial O2 and reused fuel.
sources.supports: Direction mattered for these measured front speeds.
sources.limits: Pure cellulose, PE and other assemblies cannot inherit either speed. Flame length and spread speed are distinct.
